# Plot main metadata table

```{r}
dat2 <- as.data.frame(read_excel("../data/raw/data_input/41586_2023_6770_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx", sheet = 2))
colnames(dat2) <- dat2[1, ]
dat2 <- dat2[-1, ]
# rename the 'Only-Africa dataset' column
colnames(dat2)[which(colnames(dat2) == "Only-Africa dataset")] <- "Africa"
# include only entries in Africa
dat2 <- dat2 %>%
  filter(Africa == "Yes")
# remove rows with missing lat/lon
dat2 <- dat2 %>%
  filter(!is.na(Latitude) & !is.na(Longitude))
# transform to sf object
dat2 <- st_as_sf(dat2, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326)
# make sample size numeric
dat2$N <- as.numeric(dat2$N)
# create plot of Africa
africa <- ne_countries(continent = c("Africa"), scale = 50, returnclass = "sf")
# plot by sample size
p2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = africa) +
  geom_sf(data = dat2, aes(color = N), size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c()
p2
# plot by group
p3 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = africa) +
  geom_sf(data = dat2, aes(color = Group), size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))
p3
# plot by country
p4 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = africa) +
  geom_sf(data = dat2, aes(color = Country), size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))
p4
#grid.arrange(p2, p3, p4, ncol = 1)

# 
```

The metadata plotted above contain 111 populations - the data in the 'Only African' dataset in Fortez-Lima et al 2023.

I suspect we have some data data from the 'Full-genotyped' dataset as this contains '81 populations with sample sizes lower than 10 individuals'

# Merge metadata

```{r}
all_pops <- rbind(dat2, dat3, dat4, dat10)
dups <- duplicated(all_pops)
# remove duplicates
all_pops <- all_pops[!dups, ]
```

Coordinates are available for 136 populations after merging the metadata.

However, setdiff shows 106 of the populations in NEO_full are not in the metadata!

```{r}
setdiff(NEO_full$population, all_pops$Population)
```

In some cases the mismatch is a naming issue, eg

 - Namibia_DamaraKSP in dat$`Population label` is probably "Namibia_Damara" in NEO_full)
 - There are coords for Sotho, but in NEO_full there are southern and northern Sotho...
 - SouthAfrica_Coloured in NEO_full is probably SouthAfrica_ColouredAskham in dat$`Population label` - both have 12 individuals

# Fix some naming issues

```{r}
all_pops$Population <- ifelse(all_pops$Population == "Tanzania_TanzaniaMixed",
  "Tanzania_Mixed",
  all_pops$Population
)

# rename DRC_Bangubangu to DRC_BanguBangu in NEO_full$population
NEO_full$population <- ifelse(NEO_full$population == "DRC_Bangubangu",
  "DRC_BanguBangu",
  NEO_full$population
)

setdiff(NEO_full$population, all_pops$Population)
```

# Plot populations with genetic data AND coordinates

```{r}
# add coordinates to NEO_full based on matching population labels
NEO_full_na_omit <- NEO_full %>%
  filter(population %in% all_pops$Population)

# add geometry to NEO_full_na_omit based on matching population labels
NEO_full_na_omit <- NEO_full_na_omit %>%
  left_join(all_pops,
    by = c("population" = "Population")
  )

NEO_full_na_omit <- gt_add_sf(NEO_full_na_omit,
  coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = st_crs(4326)
)


africa <- ne_countries(continent = c("Africa"), scale = 50, returnclass = "sf")

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = africa) +
  geom_sf(data = NEO_full_na_omit$geometry, aes(colour = NEO_full_na_omit$dataset)) +

```

Given this, we can't use coordinates very easily to merge populations.

# Potential alternative groupings

- Glottocode and Guthrie group are not available for all populations, don't group on this basis.

A few options:

## 1. Group by linguistic group

For the Bantu speaking groups, each population is given a 'branch', and for the non-Bantu groups, we could use prexisting groups. This results in very unbalanced sample sizes (highest is Eastern Bantu-speaking at 1580 individuals and lowest is 23 individuals). This will also put the Mozambique individuals in a much larger Eastern Bantu-speaking group, which makes our result less specific.

```{r}
dat$`Bantu Group` <- ifelse(dat$`Bantu Group` == "-", NA, dat$`Bantu Group`)
dat$poss_group <- ifelse(!is.na(dat$`Bantu Group`), dat$`Bantu Group`, dat$Group)
table(dat$poss_group)

label_data <- dat %>%
  group_by(poss_group) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(N), geometry = st_centroid(st_union(geometry))) %>%
  arrange(-desc(n)) # Results in 14 groups
```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = africa) +
  geom_sf(data = dat, aes(color = poss_group), size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = label_data, force = 5, force_pull = 1, aes(label = n, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates", size = 3, color = "black", alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))
```

## 2. Use linguistic groups to guide cases where we merge populations together

eg if a set of populations have less than X individuals each, are part of the same linguistic branch, and within X distance of one another then we put them together. 

If a population has 15 or fewer individuals, we look for other populations within 500km that are part of the same linguistic group and save them as potential merge candidates

```{r}
distance_matrix <- st_distance(dat)
rownames(distance_matrix) <- dat$Population
colnames(distance_matrix) <- dat$Population
distance_matrix <- distance_matrix / 1000


merge_pop_names <- function(x, distance_matrix, dat) {
  # if n <= 10
  if (as.integer(x["N"]) <= 15) {
    # get the name of the population
    pop_name <- x["Population"]
    # get the group of the population
    group <- x["poss_group"]
    # find this row in the distance matrix
    dists <- distance_matrix[pop_name, ]
    # drop units
    dists <- units::drop_units(dists)
    # get the names of populations within 500km
    close_pops <- names(dists[dists <= 500])
    # exclude self-distance
    close_pops <- close_pops[close_pops != pop_name]
    # get the group of populations within 200km
    close_pops_groups <- dat$poss_group[dat$Population %in% close_pops]
    # if any pops are closer than 200 km, and within the same poss_group
    if (length(close_pops_groups > 0) & any(close_pops_groups == group)) {
      # return the names of the populations to merge
      return(paste(c(pop_name, close_pops[close_pops_groups == group]), collapse = "; "))
    } else {
      # if there's nothing it can be merged with within 200km
      return("Nothing to merge")
    }
  } else if (x["N"] > 10) {
    return(NA)
  }
}

dat$merge_names <- apply(st_drop_geometry(dat), 1, merge_pop_names,
  distance_matrix = distance_matrix, dat = dat
)

# NB consider two Baka entries with the same Population and Group
```

## Recording R environment

Part of ensuring our workflow is reproducible is to keep track of the R environment.
We will automatically save our R environment into a file called `r_environment.json`.

```{r save-r-environment, echo=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
filename_rmd <- "s10_b_map_grouping.Rmd"
filename_renv <- paste0(
  res_dir, "/renv_",
  tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(filename_rmd)),
  ".json"
)
renv::lockfile_write(renv::lockfile_create(), file = filename_renv)

```
